component.name: veetee
component.summary: DEC VT terminal for OpenVMS and other DEC hosts

description.p: veetee emulates DEC video terminals, from the VT52 and VT100 to the VT420 and the colour VT525, as faithfully as the manuals allow: DEC factory Set-Up defaults, fonts drawn on DEC's own character cells, and the control functions forms and editing applications rely on.

ul.li: VT100 to VT525 emulation with pages, rectangles, soft fonts, national character sets and dual sessions
An LK401 keyboard layout with PF1–PF4, the editing keypad and user-defined keys
Telnet, SSH, serial lines and local shells
The terminal's own Set-Up, keyclick and bells, smooth scrolling and a CRT picture
Saved connections, session logs, a searchable history and screen reader support

screenshot.caption: A forms application on the VT420 model

description.p: Kermit file transfer, in the window and from the command line, and a long paste no longer ends a LAT session.
A saved connection can be made the default, opened when veetee starts without a connection.
A LAT terminal no longer goes dead a few minutes into every session.
A LAT session no longer freezes with the screen stopped and the keys still clicking.
A LAT session survives a wire that loses frames, and a window with two sessions can get back to one.
veetee 1.0: the VT52 through the colour VT525, on Linux and Windows.
Releases carry an RPM as well as a Debian package, a tarball and a Flatpak.
LAT connections pick an interface from a list, and RFC 2217 is proved against a real server.
Says what to do when LAT cannot open a socket, and lets the command be copied.
veetee speaks LAT, so an OpenVMS node can be reached over DEC's own protocol.
veetee can find the LAT services announcing themselves on a wire, on Linux.
Selections can be dragged out of the scrollback, and Telnet can set up a terminal server's line.
Idle Telnet sessions are no longer dropped, and Scroll Lock is now the Do key.
VT100 mode no longer makes the terminal report itself as a VT102.
OpenVMS: Backspace deletes again over Telnet, and editors no longer lose the line after a long one.
Windows: veetee starts on computers whose graphics driver left an old Vulkan loader in place.
Local shells and SSH work properly in the Flatpak: shells get job control and SSH can ask for passwords.
Screen reader support, output about three times faster, and a Flatpak bundle.
Saved connections, session logs, history review and search, and copy and paste that translate DEC characters.
The VT500 menu Set-Up, Display Controls, and hand-drawn 48-line and 132-column fonts.
